headline: NASA launches emergency mission to save Swift Observatory from crashing to Earth
summary: Launched in 2004, the Swift Observatory is in danger of burning up in Earth's atmosphere due to recent solar storms. An emergency mission aims to boost its orbit.
details: The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, launched in 2004, is at risk of crashing to Earth as early as this year due to its orbit being lowered by recent solar storms. NASA has partnered with Katalyst Space Technologies for an emergency mission to prevent its demise.

Katalyst's Link spacecraft launched Friday with the objective of intercepting Swift, which lacks its own propulsion system. The mission aims to boost Swift's orbit by approximately 150 miles, raising it from its current altitude of 224 miles.

The mission was expedited due to a critical deadline: Swift would be too low to save by October. Katalyst developed the solution in just nine months, with the mission costing $30 million to save the $500 million observatory.
The Swift Observatory is crucial for studying gamma-ray bursts, which provide vital insights into the early universe. This rescue mission ensures its continued scientific contributions.

headline: AI agents can now pay for skills using x402 and AP2 mandates
summary: MarketNow implements autonomous agent payments on Base using USDC and delegated mandates, enabling AI agents to transact for services without human intervention.
details: AI agents require the ability to purchase skills and services autonomously. MarketNow has implemented a system for agent-to-agent payments using x402 (HTTP 402 Payment Required) and AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol) delegated mandates.
When an agent requests a paid skill without payment, the system returns an HTTP 402 error. The agent then reads the headers, sends USDC, and retries the request with a transaction hash (txHash).

Payment verification is handled by calling eth_getTransactionReceipt on the Base network. Each txHash can only be used once, and used txHashes are persisted as files in a GitHub repository for tracking.
Before an agent can make purchases, a human principal must create a mandate, which includes defined spending limits to ensure security and control over transactions.
The implementation underwent a security audit, which identified four critical issues that were subsequently addressed. MarketNow aims to provide a trust layer for agent commerce.
